title: Article 176 — Special address by the Governor

content.overview: Article 176 — Special address by the Governor. Complete constitutional treatise with procedural anchors, cases, and chamber drafting blueprints.
content.study:
Topic at a Glance
Article 176 of the Constitution of India is titled “Special address by the Governor”. It forms an integral component of The States (Articles 152–237), located within the “The States” cluster. Current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023.

Constitutional Text & Anatomy
(1) At the commencement of the first session after each general election to the Legislative Assembly and at the commencement of the first session of each year], the Governor shall address the Legislative Assembly or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, both Houses assembled together and inform the Legislature of the causes of its summons.

(2) Provision shall be made by the rules regulating the procedure of the House or either House for the allotment of time for discussion of the matters referred to in such address3 [omitted . . House\
